The 1% rule is dead. Here's what replaced it.

The old shortcut: a rental should rent for 1% of its price each month. A $300K house → $3,000/mo.

In a lot of markets today, that house rents for closer to $2,000 (0.67%). And the rule never accounted for the things that decide whether a rental makes money: the interest rate, insurance, taxes, repairs and vacancy.

The replacement is simple: real monthly cash flow.
• Rent: $2,000
• Mortgage ($225K loan, 7%, 30 yr): −$1,497
• Taxes + insurance: −$450
• Repairs, vacancy, CapEx: −$300
= −$247/mo

On the same house, break-even is a price of about $250K. The rule isn't the problem. The price is.

Example numbers for illustration only.
